# HAND-BUILT FIXTURE — written from the ruled table `zypper list-updates`
# produces on a serviceable Leap release (zypper(8), same command as the
# Tumbleweed fixture). It is not a transcript of a real system's output: no row
# below was recorded from a running openSUSE install, and the versions were
# written by hand to the shape Leap's update repositories use
# (`<upstream>-<solvable revision>`, e.g. `2.31-150300.10.1`).
#
# Still owed before this format can be called field-proven: a real run on
# openSUSE Leap, recorded with `LC_ALL=C zypper --non-interactive -q lu >
# fixture.txt`.
#
# This fixture carries the OTHER column layout the parser is written to
# tolerate: an Arch column where a newer zypper prints Status, and rows whose
# padding is ragged because zypper fits columns to the widest cell it has. A
# serviceable Leap keeps every released update in its repositories, which is
# also why the rollback in zypper.go can usually still resolve the version
# recorded for it here — unlike a rolling Tumbleweed snapshot.
